summary: Implemented src/loaders/partials-loader.ts — loadPartials(dir: string): Promise<Record<string, string>>. Reads all .md files in a directory with readdir/readFile (node:fs/promises), keys by filename stem, returns map. Uses path.join for cross-platform safety.

Implemented src/loaders/metadata-loader.ts — discoverPersonaYamls(root) uses readdir with { recursive: true } (Node ≥ 18.17) to return sorted absolute paths of all *.yaml files; loadMetadata(yamlPath) reads YAML with js-yaml, validates result is a non-null object with a non-empty string 'name' field, returns typed PersonaMetadata.
Implemented src/loaders/content-loader.ts — loadContent(mdPath): Promise<string> reads a markdown file as raw UTF-8 string via readFile, no transformations applied.
Created src/loaders/index.ts barrel export for all three loader modules.
Updated src/index.ts to uncomment and activate loader exports via src/loaders/index.js.

Wrote 40 unit tests across 3 test files (partials-loader.test.ts: 10 tests, metadata-loader.test.ts: 20 tests, content-loader.test.ts: 10 tests). All use real temp directories to exercise actual fs I/O with no path-separator assumptions.
tsc --noEmit: zero errors. npm test: 141 tests passed (0 failed) across 9 test files.

comments.note: src/loaders/partials-loader.ts uses Promise.all for parallel reads, which is good for throughput. No issues found — implementation is clean, minimal, and consistent with the engine layer's style.

src/loaders/metadata-loader.ts: the PersonaMetadata type is re-exported from metadata-loader.ts for convenience, but it is defined in src/plugins/types.ts. This creates a single source of truth for the type. No duplication.

readdir with { recursive: true } requires Node ≥ 18.17. The package.json engines field already declares 'node: >=18.0.0'. This is a minor mismatch (18.0 < 18.17). Worth bumping to >=18.17 in a follow-up to accurately reflect the minimum required version.
src/loaders/ follows the same barrel-export pattern (index.ts) as src/engine/ and src/plugins/. Consistent with project conventions.

summary: Full Verification Stack executed against WP-004 (Loaders — File I/O Layer) in the ai-persona-builder-STABLE project.
Build check: tsc --noEmit exited 0 — zero TypeScript strict-mode errors across all loader source files.
Test suite: npm test (vitest run) → 141/141 tests passed across 9 test files (0 failures). Loader tests: partials-loader 10/10, metadata-loader 20/20, content-loader 10/10.

AC-1 VERIFIED: loadPartials() returns Record<string, string> keyed by filename stem. Runtime probe confirmed plain-object return with string values; isFile() guard correctly excludes directories named *.md.

AC-2 VERIFIED: discoverPersonaYamls() returns sorted absolute paths for all *.yaml files recursively. Probed: top-level files, nested (4-level deep) subdirectories, .yml files excluded, results are absolute (path.isAbsolute === true).

AC-3 VERIFIED: loadMetadata() returns typed PersonaMetadata via js-yaml. Probed: full field round-trip, whitespace-only name throws, empty YAML throws, array YAML throws, scalar YAML throws, extra fields preserved via index signature.
AC-4 VERIFIED: loadContent() returns raw string content unchanged. Probed: no trimming, no template substitution, empty file, Unicode (日本語/emoji), multiline content preserved byte-for-byte.

AC-5 VERIFIED: All tests use real temp directories (os.tmpdir) and path.join-constructed paths — no hard-coded separators. Edge-case probes confirmed path-separator independence under Node 25 (macOS POSIX). Windows path-separator divergence in discoverPersonaYamls (readdir recursive returns OS-native separators on Windows) is handled correctly by path.join(absRoot, entry) which normalises to the platform's separator.
AC-6 VERIFIED: tsc --noEmit (strict: true in tsconfig.json) reports zero errors. Confirmed strict flag is set.

comments.note: dist/index.cjs was stale at QA start — did not include loader exports. Running npm run build before runtime probes was required. This is expected (dev workflow, dist is rebuilt on demand), not a defect. All loader functions (loadPartials, discoverPersonaYamls, loadMetadata, loadContent) are present in the freshly built dist.

Confirmed pre-existing debt: package.json engines field declares 'node: >=18.0.0' but readdir with { recursive: true } requires Node >=18.17. Developer already flagged this. Worth bumping to >=18.17 in a follow-up to accurately reflect the true minimum runtime requirement.

discoverPersonaYamls uses path.join(absRoot, entry) where entry comes from recursive readdir. On Windows, recursive readdir returns paths with backslash separators in the relative portion; path.join handles normalisation correctly because absRoot is already resolved. Design is sound — no action needed.
loadPartials correctly uses withFileTypes: true and entry.isFile() guard, preventing directories named *.md from appearing as partial keys. Edge-case probe confirmed. No issues.

summary: Reviewed 5 source files (partials-loader.ts, metadata-loader.ts, content-loader.ts, loaders/index.ts, src/index.ts) plus package.json. 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Medium, 2 Low findings. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: MEDIUM | A01 — Broken Access Control (Path Traversal risk — caller-trust boundary). All three loaders (loadPartials, discoverPersonaYamls, loadContent) accept caller-supplied path strings and pass them directly to fs/promises APIs with no path-containment validation. In the current design this is acceptable — these are build-time library functions invoked with developer-controlled paths, not user-supplied input. However, if any future layer accepts paths from an HTTP request, CLI argument without sanitisation, or plugin-provided data, a path-traversal attack becomes trivially possible (e.g. '../../etc/passwd'). The risk is rated Medium rather than High because: (1) the library has no HTTP surface today; (2) the README/API contract does not expose these functions to untrusted input. Recommendation: document the caller-trust assumption explicitly in each loader's JSDoc, and add a path-containment guard (e.g. ensure path.resolve(input) starts with an allowed root prefix) if these functions are ever exposed to untrusted input. File refs: src/loaders/partials-loader.ts L35, src/loaders/metadata-loader.ts L47 / L85, src/loaders/content-loader.ts L33.

LOW | A06 — Vulnerable & Outdated Components (engines field mismatch). package.json declares 'node: >=18.0.0' but readdir with { recursive: true } requires Node >=18.17.0. This creates a window where a consumer running Node 18.0–18.16 receives a runtime TypeError rather than a clear version error. Not a direct security vulnerability, but could facilitate supply-chain confusion or unexpected runtime failures on older CI runners. Recommendation: bump engines.node to '>=18.17.0'. File ref: package.json L39-41.

LOW | A04 — Insecure Design (YAML deserialization — js-yaml safe load confirmed). loadMetadata uses yaml.load() from js-yaml v4. In js-yaml v4, load() is the safe loader (the unsafe loadUnsafe/loadAll with custom types was removed). No JavaScript code execution via YAML is possible with this API. Additionally, the parsed result is validated: non-null, non-array object with a required 'name' string field. The remaining fields pass through via the index signature [key: string]: unknown — consumers receive unvalidated unknown values for extra fields, but this is appropriate for a schema-open metadata format. No action required; recorded for awareness. File ref: src/loaders/metadata-loader.ts L88.

No secrets, credentials, API keys, or hardcoded sensitive data found in any reviewed file. No network I/O performed (all operations are local fs reads). No authentication or session management surface. No logging calls that could leak sensitive data. No use of eval, Function constructor, child_process, or dynamic require. All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed: A01 (Medium noted above), A02 (N/A — no crypto), A03 (N/A — no interpreter input), A04 (Low noted above), A05 (N/A — no server config), A06 (Low noted above), A07 (N/A — no auth), A08 (N/A — no deserialization beyond yaml.load safe), A09 (N/A — no logging surface), A10 (N/A — no server-side HTTP requests).

notes: All 6 acceptance criteria met. 40 new loader tests pass; full suite (141 tests) green. TypeScript strict-mode clean. Key design notes for QA: (1) loadPartials uses readdir withFileTypes for efficiency; (2) discoverPersonaYamls uses readdir recursive (Node ≥18.17) — no glob lib needed; (3) loadMetadata validates parsed YAML is a non-null, non-array object with a non-empty string 'name' field and throws descriptive errors otherwise; (4) loadContent is minimal — raw fs read, no transforms; (5) all paths constructed with path.join/path.resolve for cross-platform correctness; (6) tests use real temp directories (os.tmpdir), no fs mocking.

All 6 ACs met and verified by QA. 141/141 tests pass; tsc --noEmit clean. No blocking issues. One low-priority debt to flag for code review: package.json engines field should be bumped from >=18.0.0 to >=18.17.0 to accurately reflect the readdir { recursive: true } requirement.

Security audit PASS. 0 Critical/High findings — no blockers. Two low-priority observations forwarded for code review: (1) caller-trust path-traversal assumption should be documented in JSDoc (Medium risk, acceptable for build-time library); (2) package.json engines.node should be bumped to >=18.17.0 (pre-existing debt, already noted by Developer and QA). All 6 acceptance criteria confirmed met.
